metadata.title: Rubrik Quarantine Files
metadata.description: This playbook is an HTTP Request-triggered child playbook that quarantines a batch of files reported by a Rubrik Security Cloud DSPM violation. It is called by the RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation playbook with the whole files array in a single call and iterates internally, so it runs once per incident instead of once per file. It branches on objectType into three paths: ONEDRIVE files are quarantined via Microsoft Graph (the analyst is asked once per run for a quarantine folder name via a Teams Adaptive Card, then each file is searched, downloaded, uploaded to the resolved folder, and the source deleted only after a confirmed upload); NTFS (WINDOWS_FILESHARE) files are quarantined via Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (the device is resolved by physicalHost, each file's SHA1 is resolved via advanced hunting, and a StopAndQuarantineFile machine action is created and polled); any other objectType returns NotImplemented. A single app registration (client id/secret in Key Vault) authenticates both Microsoft Graph and MDE; only the OAuth2 token scope differs per branch. The playbook returns { status, results: [ { filename, status, newLocation, error } ] } to the caller.
prerequisites: 1. A single Azure AD app registration is used for BOTH Microsoft Graph and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Grant it (all admin-consented):
a. Microsoft Graph APPLICATION permissions: Files.ReadWrite.All, Sites.ReadWrite.All, User.Read.All.
b. WindowsDefenderATP (Microsoft Defender for Endpoint) APPLICATION permissions: Machine.ReadWrite.All (or Machine.StopAndQuarantine) and AdvancedQuery.Read.All.
2. Store the app registration credentials in Key Vault and obtain the Key Vault name and tenantId.
a. Create a Key Vault with a unique name.

b. Go to KeyVault -> secrets, click Generate/import and create the secrets named by GraphClientIdSecretName and GraphClientSecretSecretName (defaults 'Graph-App-ClientId' and 'Graph-App-ClientSecret') for storing client_id and client_secret respectively. These same credentials authenticate both Graph and MDE.
NOTE: Make sure the Permission model in the Access Configuration of the Key Vault is set to 'Vault access policy'. If not, change it to 'Vault access policy'.
3. For the ONEDRIVE branch, a Microsoft Teams team and channel are required for the folder-name Adaptive Card.
4. For the NTFS branch, the target file shares must be hosted on devices onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and resolvable by their physicalHost / computerDnsName.

5. This playbook is a prerequisite for the RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation playbook and must be deployed first, in the same resource group. RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation calls this playbook as a sub-playbook (via its RubrikQuarantineFilesPlaybookName parameter) once per incident to quarantine the violation files.
postDeployment: **a. Authorize connections**
Once deployment is complete, authorize each connection.
1. Go to your logic app -> API connections -> Select the Teams connection resource.
2. Go to General -> edit API connection.
3. Click Authorize.
4. Sign in.
5. Click Save.
6. The Key Vault connection uses the managed identity and does not require an interactive sign-in.
**b. Assign Role to comment on and update incidents (if the caller requires it)**
1. Go to Log Analytics Workspace -> <your workspace> -> Access Control -> Add.
2. Add role assignment.
3. Assignment type: Job function roles.
4. Role: Microsoft Sentinel Responder.
5. Members: select managed identity for assigned access to and add your logic app as member.
6. Click on review + assign.
**c. Add Access policy in Key Vault**
Add an access policy for the playbook's managed identity to read the app-registration secrets.
1. Go to logic app -> <your logic app> -> Identity -> System assigned managed identity and copy the Object (principal) ID.
2. Go to keyvaults -> <your keyvault> -> Access policies -> Create.
3. Select Get on secrets permissions. Click next.
4. In the principal section, search by the copied object ID. Click next.
5. Click review + create.
**d. Grant the app registration API permissions**
1. In Entra ID -> App registrations -> <your app> -> API permissions, add the Microsoft Graph and WindowsDefenderATP application permissions listed in the prerequisites and grant admin consent.
2. For the NTFS branch, ensure the file-share hosts are onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and resolvable by their physicalHost / computerDnsName.
**e. Configurations in Microsoft Sentinel**
1. This playbook has an HTTP Request trigger and is invoked by RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation; it does not attach directly to an automation rule.

2. Deploy this playbook before RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation. When deploying RubrikDSPMViolationRemediation, set its RubrikQuarantineFilesPlaybookName parameter to this Logic App's name so it can call this sub-playbook.

metadata.description: Name of the Logic App / playbook resource. Must match RubrikQuarantineFilesPlaybookName on the caller.
Microsoft Teams team (group) ID where the folder-name Adaptive Card is posted.
Microsoft Teams channel ID (within TeamsGroupId) for the folder-name Adaptive Card.
Key Vault holding the Graph app registration client id and secret.
Azure AD tenant ID used for the Microsoft Graph OAuth2 token endpoint.
Key Vault secret name holding the Graph app registration client id.
Key Vault secret name holding the Graph app registration client secret.

REQUIRED. ISO 3166-1 region code required by Microsoft Graph /search/query for application (app-only) permissions. Must match the tenant's data location (e.g. NAM, EUR, GBR, APC, AUS, CAN, IND, JPN). Without it Graph returns 'Region is required when request with application permission.'

inputs.name: Failure_Message
inputs.value: Failed to acquire a Microsoft Graph token (status @{coalesce(outputs('Get_Graph_Token')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Verify the app registration credentials in Key Vault and the tenant id.

body.text: Enter the quarantine folder name. @{length(coalesce(triggerBody()?['files'], json('[]')))} file(s) will be moved into a folder with this name in the same drive (OneDrive or SharePoint document library) where each file is located. The folder is created in that drive if it does not already exist.

value.error: Failed to search for the file in OneDrive (Graph status @{coalesce(outputs('Search_file')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). @{string(coalesce(body('Search_file'), ''))}

Found the file but failed to resolve or create the quarantine folder in its OneDrive (lookup status @{coalesce(outputs('Get_quarantine_folder')?['statusCode'], 'none')}, create status @{coalesce(outputs('Create_quarantine_folder')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Source NOT deleted. @{string(coalesce(body('Create_quarantine_folder'), ''))}
Found the file but failed to download its content from OneDrive (Graph status @{coalesce(outputs('Download_file_content')?['statusCode'], 'none')}).
Found the file but failed to fetch its content from the OneDrive download URL (status @{coalesce(outputs('Fetch_download_url')?['statusCode'], 'none')}).

Downloaded the file but failed to upload it to the quarantine folder (Graph status @{coalesce(outputs('Upload_file')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Source NOT deleted. @{string(coalesce(body('Upload_file'), ''))}

@if(and(greaterOrEquals(coalesce(outputs('Delete_source_file')?['statusCode'], 0), 200), less(coalesce(outputs('Delete_source_file')?['statusCode'], 0), 300)), '', concat('Uploaded to quarantine but failed to delete the source (Graph status ', string(coalesce(outputs('Delete_source_file')?['statusCode'], 'none')), '); delete manually.'))
Upload to the quarantine folder could not be confirmed (Graph status @{coalesce(outputs('Upload_file')?['statusCode'], 'none')}, no item id returned). Source NOT deleted.
File not found in OneDrive via Graph search.

inputs.name: Failure_Message
inputs.value: Failed to acquire a Microsoft Defender for Endpoint token (status @{coalesce(outputs('Get_MDE_Token')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Verify the app registration has WindowsDefenderATP application permissions and the credentials in Key Vault.

value.error: No physicalHost was provided for this NTFS file; cannot resolve the MDE device to quarantine it.

Could not resolve the file-share host '@{items('For_each_ntfs_file')?['physicalHost']}' in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (status @{coalesce(outputs('Get_MDE_Machine')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). Ensure the host is onboarded to MDE.

body.Query: DeviceFileEvents | where DeviceId == '@{replace(coalesce(variables('MDE_Machine_Id'), ''), '''', '''''')}' and FileName == '@{replace(coalesce(items('For_each_ntfs_file')?['filename'], ''), '''', '''''')}' and isnotempty(SHA1) | top 1 by Timestamp desc | project SHA1

value.error: Could not resolve a SHA1 for the file via MDE advanced hunting (status @{coalesce(outputs('Run_advanced_hunting_for_sha1')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). The file may not have been observed by MDE on host '@{items('For_each_ntfs_file')?['physicalHost']}'; not quarantined.
Failed to create the MDE StopAndQuarantineFile action (status @{coalesce(outputs('Create_stop_and_quarantine')?['statusCode'], 'none')}). @{string(coalesce(body('Create_stop_and_quarantine'), ''))}
MDE StopAndQuarantineFile action did not succeed within the timeout (final status @{coalesce(body('Get_action_status')?['status'], 'Unknown')}).
